title: bug: every seat registers as worker.type=CLAUDE even when its wrapper launched codex/gemini/grok
description:
Observed 2026-10-25: worker-e8965f51 and worker-9cda703c show `type: "CLAUDE"` in moe.list_workers, but their wrappers launched the Codex CLI (process argv `codex …`, tool inventory apply_patch/exec_command, no Claude Edit/Write). architect-473624b4 was a Codex TUI shown as CLAUDE. Root cause: auto-registration hardcodes the type. See packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts:650 (`const workerType: WorkerType = 'CLAUDE';`) and tools/joinTeam.ts:31 (`type: 'CLAUDE'`), although types/schema.ts:28 defines WorkerType = 'CLAUDE' | 'CODEX' | 'GEMINI' | 'GROK'.

Impact: governors and humans cannot tell which seats can produce the Claude-only TOOL witness. scripts/moe-agent.sh:3567 requires that witness to land a contested path, and its stream collector is Claude-only. Four delivery gaps on 2026-10-24/25 (M01 CONFIGURATION.md, ab6aac94 SCHEMA.md, c2cb5cf7, 5f3960df postflight.sh) involved seats whose label hid that they couldn't witness. Diagnosing them meant mapping /proc/*/environ MOE_WORKER_ID to argv by hand.

Expected: the wrapper, which knows the CLI it launches, reports it. moe-proxy forwards it the way it injects workerId. The daemon records it on registration, validated against WorkerType, and refreshes it when a seat relaunches under a different CLI. list_workers / chat_who then show the real type. Keep both launchers in parity.
definitionOfDone: A seat launched by scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} with codex, gemini or grok registers with worker.type CODEX, GEMINI or GROK respectively, and a claude seat registers CLAUDE; covered by daemon tests for claim_next_task and join_team registration.

A seat whose wrapper relaunches it under a different CLI has its recorded type updated on the next claim/registration, and an unknown or missing type keeps today's CLAUDE default without failing the call.
moe-proxy forwards the launcher-provided type the same way it injects workerId, with a proxy test; both launchers set it, and `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` stays green.
Fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` and the proxy's `npm test` exit 0, with output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.note: New packages/moe-proxy/src/workerType.integration.test.ts (~170 lines). Each launch spawns the built proxy (dist/index.js) against an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 WebSocketServer. The server dispatches frames in arrival order into the daemon's real McpAdapter.handle over a ToolTestHarness StateManager on a temp project, with daemon.json written there. The daemon modules load via a computed dynamic import, so tsc (rootDir src) never compiles daemon source. LOG_LEVEL=silent and MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE=nonexistent are set for the in-process daemon and restored in afterAll; vitest.config.ts already blanks inherited MOE_* identity. Cases: each of the 4 types, with explicit-workerId join+claim and no workerType, is persisted in memory and on disk, assigned task-1, kept in the team, and projected by list_workers and chat_who. GROK runs under MOE_TOOL_NAME_STYLE=underscore with moe_ names, which covers the alias path. A relaunch CODEX -> GEMINI (claim, alreadyAssigned) -> GROK (join) refreshes the type and keeps the task and membership; an absent-env relaunch keeps GROK. Absent, lowercase 'codex' and 'OPENAI' each register a new seat as CLAUDE and the claim still succeeds. Error handling: replies waited for at most 10 s (stderr in the message); an error reply or missing text fails the test; stdin end, then SIGKILL after 3 s, in finally; server closed and temp dir removed in afterEach. Run in the git-archive snapshot /tmp/bdf6-snap (HEAD e7b84cc + owned files, native npm ci, node 24.21.0): proxy npm test exit 0, 5 files, 176/176; this file 8/8. Mutant (proxy `typed = false`) fails the 4 typed cases, restored + cmp. 0 leaked proxies, 0 temp dirs. The shared packages/moe-proxy/dist was not touched.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review of this diff together with f107447 (daemon) and 29216f5 (proxy), treated as one fix.
- Fixed: scripts/CLAUDE.md had dropped a connective ("MOE_RUNNER_HOST the execution identity"); it now reads "MOE_RUNNER_HOST, the execution identity … and the seat's CLI type". The gate was re-run fresh afterwards and passed (GATE_EXIT=0, same counts).
- Concurrency: every tool is dispatched under the global state mutex. refreshWorkerType skips the write when nothing changes, and passes lastActivityAt back unchanged, so there is no presence drift.
- Seats with different CLIs sharing a config: Codex gets the type only through the per-seat -c override (a value persisted in config.toml is stripped). Grok's literal `${MOE_WORKER_TYPE:-}` expands per process. Claude and gemini inherit the env. Two seats therefore cannot leak a type into each other.
- Stale values: the launcher export is unconditional, so it replaces the value after a hot reload (tested on both engines over an inherited GROK).
- Bad values: null, blank, lowercase or unknown all become CLAUDE on a new seat. An omitted key keeps the existing type. A blank env sends nothing (proxy).
- Explicit arguments: a workerId named by the call still gets the type injected; a workerType set by the caller wins.
- Both the no-work and alreadyAssigned paths refresh the type (integration test). Alias spellings (moe_/bare) are covered by the proxy set and the GROK integration case.
- Platforms: Windows argv detection is tested with .cmd/.exe paths and Git Bash. The macOS Bash 3.2 mapping uses a plain case. The integration test kills its child processes in finally (SIGKILL after 3 s).
- Compatibility: the daemon does not enforce additionalProperties, so an older daemon ignores workerType. No schema or state shape changed.
- Known, pre-existing, not fixed: when python is missing, the sh Codex fallback writes a partial MOE_WORKER_ID override with no type. That seat keeps its recorded type, or CLAUDE if new.

comments.content:
Contract fixed by the daemon prerequisite task-0b40957c (plan rev 1). Step-4's integration test must expect these:
(1) Absent or blank MOE_WORKER_TYPE: the proxy sends no workerType key. A NEW seat then registers as CLAUDE, but an EXISTING seat keeps its recorded type and nothing is written. So test "absent → CLAUDE" on a fresh seat only.

completionSummary:
Seats now register their real CLI as worker.type; the launcher side is now delivered on top of the landed daemon (f107447) and proxy (29216f5) contract.
- Both launchers export MOE_WORKER_TYPE right after CLI detection, before any pre-flight RPC: sh uses a bash-3.2 case, ps1 uses $cliType.ToUpperInvariant(). The values are CODEX, GEMINI, GROK, and CLAUDE for anything else. The export is unconditional, so it replaces an inherited value after a hot reload.

It covers all 4 types through join and claim (memory, disk, list_workers, chat_who), a relaunch CODEX→GEMINI (alreadyAssigned)→GROK (join), an absent env keeping the type, and absent, lowercase and unknown values registering CLAUDE.
